comments.author: Solid-Funny-668
comments.body:
This is a rule book and python code tool for claude and chatgpt to follow and act as a stable GM running your world.

Everything comes back to these three ideas:

* **The world doesn't revolve around the player.** Things can be found, avoided, changed, missed, or lost for good.
* **Cause comes first.** AI are force to design to create a truth before a quest and story not bent towards what every user found or suddenly imagine of.
* **Narration can't change the state.** Once truth is been set in background or save it will be fix so not sudden changes of i plan this this then change the ending is not in your favour.

[https://github.com/west132/AI-GM-Engine.git](https://github.com/west132/AI-GM-Engine.git)

comments.author: No-Pollution7797
comments.body:
The part I'd watch closest is player input that smuggles in state, like "I take out the key I found in the cellar" when no key was ever saved. Models love to go along with that, so I'd check claims like that against the save before the narration step ever sees them, not after.



Also curious what happens to truths that were set early but the player never goes near. Do they eventually drop out, or do they stay in context forever and crowd out what's actually happening?

replies.author: Solid-Funny-668
replies.body:
for this part, i set a thing call item points, it will says no generate important things that solve the mission or trouble, its set low and hard to increase. it helps in 2 way, user had no need to write detail on what they have, but also cant made things on and on.  
**Item points**

Item points let your character have already prepared for something you didn’t think of in time. You spend points, and it turns out you packed it, bought it earlier, or it’s lying within reach.

* **Pool:** depends on your social standing. Outcast 20, commoner 40, working adult 60, well off 90, elite 120. A good rest refills 1/5 of it.
* **Cost:** a small item (rope, torch) is 1. A solid item or favour (lockpicks, a bribe) is 3. Weapon or armour costs 10 or 30, and a tool or kit costs 5 or 15.
* **Use:** just say “I spend points, I had a crowbar in my bag.” The GM gives it a believable reason and deducts the points.
* **Limits:** it can’t contradict what’s already been shown, give you unique artifacts, or get back confiscated gear. If it doesn’t fit, it costs nothing.

replies.author: No-Pollution7797
replies.body: Making it something you spend instead of a flat no is a nice way around it, and tying the pool to social standing already says a lot about the character. Does resting ever turn into a way to farm points, or is rest itself costly in your setup?
